title: Benny Carter's band and Doc Cheatham
summary: Carter's discipline, Teddy Wilson in the band, Dicky Wells and Doc Cheatham's no-pressure playing.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You mentioned briefly that you played opposite his band; you didn't talk about the band at all.
Wonderful band, and great arrangements that he made. Do you remember the theme song he had, Lonesome Nights; do you know that at all?
I've heard it. He had a reputation for being a much--I don't know if the word is stricter, more disciplined bandleader.
He really would rehearse the band until it was incredibly tight.
It was, and in fact Teddy was playing piano before he went with Benny there. Cozy Cole--who were the others? The trombone player.

Dicky Wells. Benny used to play trumpet, saxophone, play trumpet--and I was a trumpet player in those days--he used the no-pressure system. He balanced it on the palm of his hand and moved all around without effort at all.
He said Doc Cheetam (phonetic spelling) turned him on to that.
Really? Doc's something else. He's a wonderful player.
And that's the way Doc plays still. He's at a forty five degree angle.
I think he was having his seventieth birthday at a club over here two or three years ago, so that makes him seventy three or seventy four now.
Unbelieveable; and he plays so well. Not many people can do that.
